Phase 2 committed and pushed as 06850e6, thanks. New Phase 14 task: while using type --paste --verify myself as the operator to message you, I hit a real bug -- pasting multi-line/multi-paragraph text (with blank-line paragraph breaks) into this VS Copilot Chat composer resulted in only a truncated fragment (just the first line) actually landing and being sent, even though verify reported success (method clipboard-paste, success true, no verify-mismatch error). It happened twice in a row with the same multi-paragraph message, and was only resolved by collapsing to a single line. Root cause is unconfirmed -- possible causes: the composer's paste handler may treat embedded newlines specially (e.g. submitting or truncating at the first newline), or GetTextForPasteVerification's TextPattern read may be racing ahead of the full multi-line paste settling into the visible text run. Please do a Pre-Build Decomposition to investigate root cause (e.g. add a short settle delay before verification reads back text, or read back via a more robust pattern, or detect and warn/retry when verified text length is suspiciously shorter than input) and propose a fix so --paste is reliable for multi-paragraph prompts.

Let me look at the paste/verify implementation before proposing a decomposition.4 tasks done## Root-Cause Analysis (before proposing fixes)

Looking at `TypeViaPaste`/`GetTextForPasteVerification` in `UiaHelper.cs`:

- `TypeViaPaste`: click → sleep 100ms → `^v` (SendKeys Ctrl+V) → sleep 100ms → done, no re-check.
- Verification reads back via `ValuePattern.Value` first, else `TextPattern.DocumentRange.GetText(-1)`, immediately after that one 100ms sleep.

The reported symptom — **verify reported success AND the message got sent** — is the key clue. A true truncation-with-mismatch would fail verify. Success + "sent" strongly suggests: the paste itself succeeded in full, verification's single read-back snapshotted the *full* text correctly, but **afterward** the composer's own paste/input handler (likely JS-driven, since this is a VS Copilot Chat composer, not a native Win32 edit control) asynchronously processed the embedded newline as a submit trigger — clearing the box to a fragment or auto-sending — *after* our one-shot verification already returned. This is a race between our single read and the target app's own async post-processing, not a synchronous truncation we could catch by reading earlier.

## Proposed Pre-Build Decomposition

**Part A — Double-read verification (detect post-verify mutation):** After the existing verify read, add a second read-back following a short additional settle delay (e.g. 250–300ms), and compare it to the first. If they differ (especially "shrunk" or now empty/short), fail with a new error code (e.g. `verify-unstable`) rather than reporting success, so this race is surfaced instead of silently passing.

**Part B — Suspicious-shrinkage heuristic:** Independent of Part A, if the (first) verified text length is materially shorter than the input length (e.g. <50%) even though it superficially "matches" some substring, flag it — this guards against partial-match false positives, not just exact mismatches.

**Part C — Documentation only:** Regardless of A/B outcome, document in `CLI_CONTRACT.md`/`KNOWN_OPEN_FINDINGS.md` that some composer-style targets may treat embedded newlines as submit triggers even via clipboard-paste (an app-side behavior, not a SendKeys artifact), and recommend `--verify` plus (with Part A) the new instability detection as mitigation — full elimination isn't possible from the automation side since it's the target app's own logic.

Want me to proceed with A+B+C as scoped, or adjust (e.g. skip B, tune delay/threshold values)?
